## Historical audit — S0242

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/audit_sources/raw_failures/scene_rsi_v2_2/r1/fixed_h/H0/fixed_version_test/commons_192968130/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; all observations are complete, not split.

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The task was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate meshes and matched camera/framing. The reference image itself is not visible in this audit. The student’s “warm compact kitchen” interpretation is an inferred scene goal, not independently verified content. |
| Student response and execute step 1, lines 3–4 | The program specified multiple objects: room shell, door and hardware, cabinets, countertop, sink, cooktop and hood. It used separate geometric pieces, including a segmented counter around a basin and separate door hardware; intended connections do not establish correct contact or alignment. There is no articulated figure or pose to assess in the code. |
| Student response, line 3 | Tile/grain and stone flecks were modeled as geometry; material settings varied roughness, metallic response and emission. The program set a 26 mm camera, four area lights and Cycles settings. These are attempted choices, not evidence that textures, viewpoint, lighting or render matched the photograph. |
| Execution result, line 5 | After 422.34 seconds, execution failed at `world.use_nodes=True`: the scene world was `None`. The result reported `image: null`; no rendered comparison or geometric validation is visible. This is a concrete build failure, not proof of visual algorithmic correctness or failure. |
| Student request and session, lines 6–9 | The student received the execution traceback and a request to revise, with about 82 seconds remaining. The next session timed out; no revised response, second execution, successful build or `DONE` is recorded. The scene loop ended in a timeout error. |

**Teacher and exploration:** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher input is present, and therefore no adoption is evidenced. The traceback was runtime feedback, not teacher advice. The first student session reported zero tool calls; the visible autonomous work was the initial program and one runner execution, not an iterative visual search (lines 2–5). The second session also reported zero tool calls and timed out (line 7).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Technical interruption followed an actual code error; formal scene success and visual correctness remain unknown. This was not an empty initial program, but no corrective patch is visible. No score or independent image verification is supplied. Whether the modeled objects, materials, part contacts, camera or lights resemble the reference cannot be determined from names and code alone.

**Lessons:** Transferably, a failed build and absent image prevent visual validation, and a long execution can leave too little time for correction. Task-specific evidence is the missing Blender world at the attempted world-node configuration; the trace does not establish why it was missing or whether changing it alone would produce a correct render.
